nodes.name: Diffusion process model for log prices
nodes.statement_short: Log prices follow $d{\bf X}_t=\mu_t dt+\Theta_t d{\bf W}_t$ with drift $\mu_t$, covolatility $\Theta_t$ and Brownian motion ${\bf W}_t$.

nodes.name: Diffusion model SDE
nodes.statement: d{\bf X}_t = \boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt + \boldsymbol{\Theta}_td{\bf W}_t, \hspace{1cm} t\in [0,1],
nodes.label: eq: Model

nodes.name: Integrated covariance (ICV) matrix
ICV definition
nodes.statement: \textrm{ICV} :=\int_0^1 \boldsymbol{\Theta}_t\boldsymbol{\Theta}_t^\mathrm{T} dt
nodes.label: eq: definition of ICV

nodes.name: Realized covariance (RCV) matrix
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we can observe the log price processes $\{X_{t_i}^{(j)}\}_{j=1}^p$ synchronously at recording time $t_i = i/n$, $i=0,1,\cdots,n$, during one trading day. Then the RCV matrix is defined as
\[\textrm{RCV} := \sum_{i=1}^n\Delta{\bf X}_i(\Delta{\bf X}_i)^{\mathrm{T}},\]
where
\[
\Delta{\bf X}_i = \begin{pmatrix}
\Delta X_i^{(1)}\\
\vdots \\
\Delta X_i^{(p)}\\
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
 X_{t_i}^{(1)} -  X_{t_{i-1}}^{(1)}\\
\vdots\\
 X_{t_i}^{(p)} -  X_{t_{i-1}}^{(p)}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: RCV is the sum of outer products of synchronous log-price increments over $n$ equally spaced times.

nodes.name: Class C processes
nodes.statement_short: A diffusion is in class $\mathcal{C}$ if its covolatility factors as $\gamma_t\Lambda$ with scalar c\`adl\`ag $\gamma_t$ and $\mathrm{tr}(\Lambda\Lambda^T)=p$.

nodes.name: Class C covolatility factorization
nodes.statement: \bm\Theta_t = \gamma_t \bm \Lambda,
nodes.label: eq: definition of Theta

nodes.name: Log prices belong to class C (Zheng and Li, Proposition 4)
nodes.statement: It has been shown that the log price process $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class ${\mathcal C}$ in Proposition 4 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011}, with the reasonable assumption that the correlation structure of $({\bf X}_t)$ does not change over a short time period.
assumptions: with the reasonable assumption that the correlation structure of $({\bf X}_t)$ does not change over a short time period
conclusions: the log price process $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class ${\mathcal C}$

nodes.name: Time-variation adjusted realized covariance (TVA) matrix
nodes.statement:
Hence, an alternative estimator has been proposed, the time-variation adjusted realized covariance (TVA) matrix, which is defined as
\[
\textrm{TVA}:= \frac{\begin{rm} tr\end{rm}(\textrm{RCV})}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\Delta{\bf X}_i(\Delta{\bf X}_i)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta{\bf X}_i|^2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: TVA rescales the sum of self-normalized outer products of increments by $\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{RCV})/n$.

nodes.name: LSD of the TVA matrix (Zheng and Li, Theorem 2)
nodes.statement:
Although the TVA matrix remains inconsistent, using random matrix theory,
Theorem 2 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011} shows that
its limiting spectral distribution depends solely on the ICV matrix through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation \eqref{eq: m-p equation} (see Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA}).
conclusions: its limiting spectral distribution depends solely on the ICV matrix through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation \eqref{eq: m-p equation}
nodes.statement_short: With one transaction per time stamp, the LSD of TVA depends only on that of ICV via the Marcenko-Pastur equation.

nodes.name: Empirical spectral distribution (ESD)
nodes.statement:
From random matrix theory, for any $p$-dimensional symmetric matrix ${\bf A}$, the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) is defined as
\begin{eqnarray} F^{{\bf A}} (x) = \dfrac 1p \sum_{j=1}^p \ {\mathbf{I}} (\lambda_j({\bf A}) \le x), ~~~~ \forall x\in \mathbb{R},
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\mathbf{I}}(\cdot)$ is an indicator function and $\lambda_j({\bf A})$ denotes the $j$th largest eigenvalue of matrix ${\bf A}$.

nodes.name: ESD formula
nodes.statement: F^{{\bf A}} (x) = \dfrac 1p \sum_{j=1}^p \ {\mathbf{I}} (\lambda_j({\bf A}) \le x), ~~~~ \forall x\in \mathbb{R},
nodes.label: eqn:ESD

nodes.name: Limiting spectral distribution (LSD)
nodes.statement: The limit of ESD is referred to as the limiting spectral distribution (LSD), if it exists.

nodes.name: Number sets and upper half-plane
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathbb{N}$ denote the sets of complex, real, integer, and natural numbers, respectively;  $\mathbb{C}^+$, a subset of $\mathbb{C}$, contains positive imaginary parts.

nodes.name: Euclidean norm notation
nodes.statement: All vectors are column vectors, and we use $|\cdot|$ to denote the Euclidean norm for vectors.

nodes.name: Spectral norm
nodes.statement: For any real matrix ${\bf A}$, $\|{\bf A}\| = \sqrt{\lambda_{\max}({\bf A}{\bf A}^{\mathrm{T}})}$ denotes its spectral norm, where $\lambda_{\max}$ is the largest eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Frobenius norm
nodes.statement: $||{\bf A}||_F = \sqrt{\begin{rm} tr\end{rm}({\bf A}{\bf A}^{{\mathrm{T}}})}$ denotes the Frobenius norm of matrix ${\bf A}$.

nodes.name: Stieltjes transform
nodes.statement:
For any distribution function $F$, $m_F(\cdot)$ denotes its Stieltjes transform defined as
\[m_F(z) = \int \frac{1}{\lambda - z}dF(\lambda), \hspace{1cm} \text{for~} z\in \mathbb{C}^+ :=\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \Im(z) > 0\},\]
where  $\Im(z)$ is the imaginary part of $z$, and
$\lfloor\cdot\rfloor$ indicates rounding down to the nearest integer.
nodes.statement_short: $m_F(z)=\int (\lambda-z)^{-1}dF(\lambda)$ for $z$ in the upper half-plane; also fixes the floor notation.

nodes.name: Multiple-transaction observation scheme
nodes.statement:
In a given time interval $[0,1]$, one trading day, for any process $({\bf V}_t)$,
suppose that $({\bf V}_t)$ can be observed at time points $t_i = i/n$ and there are $L_i (L_i\geq 1)$ transactions during each time interval $(t_{i - 1}, t_i]$, for $i = 1,\cdots, n$.

nodes.name: Transaction times and cumulative counts
nodes.statement:
Let $V_{T_{i-1}+j}$ be the $j$th observation at  transaction time $s_{T_{i-1}+j}$ during
time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$ with $T_0\equiv 0$ and $T_i=\sum_{k=1}^i L_k$, for $j=1,2,\cdots,L_i$ and $i=1,2,\cdots, n$.
That is, $L_i$ transactions at time points $\{s_{T_{i-1}+j}, j=1,2,\cdots,L_i \}$ occurred during $(t_{i-1},t_i]$, where
$t_{i-1} < s_{T_{i-1}+1} < s_{T_{i-1}+2} <
\cdots < s_{T_{i-1}+L_i}=s_{T_i} \le t_i$.
nodes.statement_short: $V_{T_{i-1}+j}$ is the $j$th of the $L_i$ observations in $(t_{i-1},t_i]$, at times $s_{T_{i-1}+j}$, with $T_i=\sum_{k\le i}L_k$.

nodes.name: Averaged multiple-transaction observation
nodes.statement:
One commonly used method to deal with multiple transactions involves taking averages of the multiple transaction prices at each time point $t_i$, that is,
\[
\overline{{\bf V}}_i = \dfrac{1}{L_i}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j}, ~~~~~
i=1,\cdots,n,
\]
and using $\overline{{\bf V}}_i$ to approximate the observation at time point $t_i$.

nodes.name: Increment of averaged prices (asymmetric triangular form)
nodes.statement:
Then the increment becomes
\begin{align}
\Delta\overline{\bf{V}}_i :&= \overline{\bf{V}}_i - \overline{\bf{V}}_{i-1}\notag \\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} {\bf V}_{T_{i-1} + j} - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}+ j}\notag\\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}}) - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-2} + j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}} ) \\
& =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_i}a_{i,j}\Delta_{i ,j}{\bf V} + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}}b_{i-1,j}\Delta_{i - 1,j}{\bf V}\notag,
\end{align}
where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i}$, $b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and
\[
\Delta_{i,j}{\bf V} := {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j-1}, ~\text{for}~~ j=1,\cdots, L_i, ~ i=1,\cdots,n,
\]
which is an asymmetric triangular form of $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf V}$.
nodes.statement_short: The averaged-price increment is a weighted sum of tick returns with weights $a_{i,j}=1-(j-1)/L_i$ and $b_{i,j}=(j-1)/L_i$.

nodes.name: Averaged increment decomposition
nodes.statement:
\Delta\overline{\bf{V}}_i :&= \overline{\bf{V}}_i - \overline{\bf{V}}_{i-1}\notag \\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} {\bf V}_{T_{i-1} + j} - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}+ j}\notag\\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}}) - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-2} + j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}} ) \\
& =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_i}a_{i,j}\Delta_{i ,j}{\bf V} + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}}b_{i-1,j}\Delta_{i - 1,j}{\bf V}\notag,
nodes.label: eqn:Delta_V

nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix
nodes.statement_short: ATVA rescales the self-normalized sum of outer products of non-overlapping averaged returns $\Delta\overline{X}_{2i}$.

nodes.name: ATVA matrix formula
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Class C log price
nodes.statement: For all $p$, $({\bf X}_t)$ is a $p$-dimensional process in class $\mathcal{C}$ for some drift process $\boldsymbol{\mu}_t = (\mu_t^{(1)},\cdots,\mu_t^{(p)})^{\mathrm{T}}$ and covolatility process $(\boldsymbol{\Theta}_t) = (\gamma_t\boldsymbol{\Lambda})$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded drift
nodes.statement: there exists a $C_0<\infty$ such that for all $p$ and all $l = 1,\cdots,p$, $|\mu_t^{(l)}|\leq C_0$ for all $t\in[0,1)$ almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded covolatility with limited dependence on W
nodes.statement: there exists a $0\leq \delta_1<1/2$ and a sequence of index sets $\mathcal{I}_p$ satisfying $\mathcal{I}_p \subset \{1,\cdots, p\}$ and $\#\mathcal{I}_p = O(p^{\delta_1})$ such that $(\gamma_t)$ may depend on ${\bf W}_t$ but only on $(W_t^{(l)}:l\in \mathcal{I}_p)$; moreover, there exists a $C_1<\infty$ such that for all $p$, $|\gamma_t|\in(1/C_1, C_1)$ for all $t\in [0,1)$, almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded individual volatilities and uniform convergence of gamma
nodes.statement: there exists $C_2<\infty$ such that for all $p$ and all $l$, the individual volatilities $\sigma_t^{(l)} = \sqrt{(\gamma_t)^2\sum_{k=1}^p(\Lambda_{lk})^2}\in (1/C_2, C_2)$ for all $t\in [0,1]$ almost surely; in addition, $(\gamma_t)$ converges uniformly to a nonzero process $(\gamma_t^*)$ that is piecewise continuous with finitely many jumps almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: ICV spectral norm growth bound
nodes.statement: there exists $C_3<\infty$ and $0\leq \delta_2 <1/2$ such that for all $p$, $||\text{ICV}|| \leq C_3p^{\delta_2}$ almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Rate condition delta1+delta2<1/2
nodes.statement: the $\delta_1$ in \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and $\delta_2$ in \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} satisfy that $\delta_1 + \delta_2 <1/2$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: LSD of Lambda Lambda^T exists
nodes.statement: almost surely, as $p\to\infty$, the ESD of $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{T}}$ converges in distribution to a probability distribution $\breve{H}$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Dimension-to-sample ratio
nodes.statement: $N = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ with $\lim_{p\to \infty} p/N \to \rho \in (0, \infty)$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Equally spaced transaction durations
nodes.statement: the transaction durations are equally spaced in each time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$, that is, $\Delta s_{i,j}: = s_{T_{i-1}+j} - s_{T_{i-1}+j-1} = 1/(nL_i)$ for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i$ and $i = 1,\cdots, n$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Independent transaction counts with moment functions
nodes.statement: $\{L_{1},\cdots, L_n\}$ is a sequence of independent positive integers independent of $({\bf X}_t)$ with $E(\frac{1}{L_i}) = f_{1, t_i}$ and $E(\frac{1}{L_i^2}) = f_{2, t_i}$ for $i = 1, \cdots, n$, where $f_{1, t}$ and $f_{2, t}$ are c\`{a}dl\`{a}g functions satisfying $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} f_{1, t} = f_{1, t}^*$, $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} f_{2, t} = f_{2, t}^*$ for $t\in [0,1]$.
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Stationary rho-mixing noise with bounded moments
nodes.statement: For all $j= 1,\cdots,p$, the noise $(\varepsilon_t^{(j)})$ is a stationary time series with mean 0 and has bounded $4\ell$th moments and $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\rho^{(j)}(r)$ satisfying $\max_{j=1,\cdots,p} \rho^{(j)}(r) = O(r^{-\ell})$ for some integer $\ell>2$;
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Pre-averaging window and dimension ratio
nodes.statement: $h =\lfloor \xi n^{\beta} \rfloor$ for some $\xi\in(0,\infty)$ and $\beta \in ((3+\ell)/(2\ell +2), 1)$, and $M = \lfloor n/(2h)\rfloor$ satisfy that $\lim_{p\to\infty} p/M = c >0$, where $\ell$ is the integer in Assumption \eqref{asm:error};
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Bounded number of transactions
nodes.statement: there exists a constant $L^*<\infty$ such that  $\sup\limits_{1\leq i \leq n} L_i\leq L^*$, almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Last transaction time near recording time
nodes.statement: $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n} n(s_{T_i} - s_{T_{i-1}}) \to 1$, almost surely, as $n\to \infty$.
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: LSD of the ATVA matrix (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement:
Suppose that Assumptions \eqref{asm:class_c}--\eqref{asm:moment_L} hold.
Then, almost surely, the ESDs of ICV and ${\mathcal A}_N$ converge to probability distributions $H$ and $F^{{\mathcal A}}$, respectively, where
\begin{equation}
H(x)=\breve{H}(x/\theta), ~~~ \textrm{for all } x\geq 0 ~ \textrm{with} ~ \theta=\int_0^1 (\gamma_t^*)^2 dt, \end{equation}
and $F^{{\mathcal A}}$ and $H$ are related as follows:
\[
m_{{\mathcal A}}(z) = \int_{\tau\in \mathbb{R}} \frac{1}{\tilde{\theta}_f/\theta\cdot\tau(1 - \rho(1 + zm_{{\mathcal A}}(z))) - z}dH(\tau), ~~~~ \textrm{for} ~ z\in \mathbb{C}^+,
\]
where  $\tilde{\theta}_f = \int_0^1 (\dfrac 13 + \dfrac 16 f_{2,s}^*)(\gamma_s^*)^2ds$ and $m_{{\mathcal A}}(z)$ denotes the Stieltjes transform of $F^{{\mathcal A}}$.
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix
conclusions: almost surely, the ESDs of ICV and ${\mathcal A}_N$ converge to probability distributions $H$ and $F^{{\mathcal A}}$, respectively
nodes.statement_short: With multiple transactions, the LSD of ATVA is tied to that of ICV through a Marcenko-Pastur equation scaled by $\tilde\theta_f/\theta$, which depends on transaction counts.
nodes.label: thm:LSD_TVA

nodes.name: LSD of ICV as rescaled breve H
nodes.statement: H(x)=\breve{H}(x/\theta), ~~~ \textrm{for all } x\geq 0 ~ \textrm{with} ~ \theta=\int_0^1 (\gamma_t^*)^2 dt,

nodes.name: Inconsistency of the scale estimator under multiple transactions
nodes.statement:
Note that if $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class $\mathcal{C}$ then the ICV matrix can be written as $\textrm{ICV} = \int_0^1 \gamma_t^2 dt\cdot \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$, where $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{T}}$.
When $L_i \equiv 1$, Theorem 2 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011} shows that the LSDs of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ and $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ are related through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation (see \eqref{eq: converfence of proposition A1}), and $2\sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta {\bf X}_{2i}|^2/p $ is a consistent estimator of $\theta=\int_0^1 (\gamma_t^*)^2 dt$.
Throughout the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:LSD_TVA} in this paper, the LSDs of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ and $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ are related through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation (see Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} in the appendix); 
 however,  $2\sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta {\bf X}_{2i}|^2/p $ is no longer consistent with $\theta$ in a general setting when $L_i \equiv 1$ is not satisfied. 
Hence, a non-overlapping A-ATVA matrix, $\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N$, is proposed in Corollary \ref{cor:LSD_ATVA}, the LSD of which depends solely on that of the ICV matrix.
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix
nodes.statement_short: Under class C, ICV is $\int\gamma_t^2dt\cdot\breve\Sigma$; the scale estimator $2\sum|\Delta X_{2i}|^2/p$ is inconsistent unless $L_i\equiv1$, motivating A-ATVA.

nodes.name: U-shaped intraday volatility and piecewise constant transaction rates
nodes.statement:
Moreover, observe that the stock intraday volatility tends to be U-shaped, which implies that the numbers of transactions at opening and closing of the market tend to be much larger than the numbers in the middle of the day.
Thus, if Assumption \eqref{asm:moment_L} is further taken to be piecewise constant, Corollary \ref{cor:LSD_ATVA} (see below) holds.
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Adjusted ATVA (A-ATVA) matrix
nodes.statement:
If we further suppose that $(f_{2, s}^*)$ is piecewise constant, that is, there exist constant numbers  $\eta_1,\cdots,\eta_K$ for $K<\infty$ such that
\[
f_{2, s}^* = \sum_{i=1}^K \eta_i  \mathrm{I}\{s\in(a_{i-1}, a_i]\},
\]
where $(0, 1] = \sum_{i =1}^K (a_{i-1}, a_i]$ and $0 = a_{0} <a_1<\cdots<a_K = 1$, then we define the adjusted ATVA (A-ATVA) matrix as
\[
\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N := \frac{1}{p}\sum_{i = 1}^K \left( \dfrac13 + \frac{1}{6(\ell_i - \ell_{i-1})}\sum_{j = \ell_{i-1}+1}^{\ell_i}\frac{1}{L_j^2}\right)^{-1} \sum_{m = \lfloor (\ell_{i-1} + 1)/2\rfloor + 1}^{\lfloor\ell_i/2\rfloor}|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2m}|^2
\cdot \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}},
\]
where $\ell_i = \max\limits_{0\leq j\leq n}j/n\leq a_i$, provided that $\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq K}n(a_i - a_{i-1})\geq 3$.

nodes.statement_short: A-ATVA rescales $\widetilde\Sigma$ blockwise by the inverse of $1/3+\frac16\overline{L^{-2}}$ to remove the transaction-count effect.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.1
nodes.statement: A direct consequence of Theorem \ref{thm:LSD_TVA} is the following corollary, which demonstrates that the LSD of the A-ATVA matrix $\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N $ depends solely on that of the ICV through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation.

nodes.name: LSD of the A-ATVA matrix (Corollary 2.1)
nodes.statement:
Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:LSD_TVA}, if we further suppose that $(f_{2, s}^*)$ is piecewise constant, then, almost surely, the ESD of $\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N $ converges to a probability distribution $F^{\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}}$, which is determined by $H$ through the Stieltjes transform via the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation
\[
m_{\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}}(z) = \int  \frac{1}{\tau(1 - \rho(1 + zm_{\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}}(z))) - z}dH(\tau), ~~~~ \textrm{for} ~ z\in \mathbb{C}^+,
\]
where $m_{\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}}(z)$ is the Stieltjes transform of $F^{\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}}$.

and the pre-averaging averaged observation becomes
\[

\]

nodes.name: Scale estimator theta-hat
nodes.statement: It was shown in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA} that $\hat\theta_p = 3\sum_{i = 1}^M |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2/p$ is a consistent estimator of $\theta = \lim_{p\to\infty}\int_0^1 \gamma_t^2dt$, and the LSDs of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}} = p/M \cdot \sum_{i = 1}^M\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} (\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{{\mathrm{T}}}/|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2 $ and $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ are related through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation \eqref{eq: m-p equation}.
nodes.statement_short: $\hat\theta_p=3\sum|\Delta\widetilde{\overline Y}_{2i}|^2/p$ consistently estimates $\theta$; $\widetilde\Xi$ and $\breve\Sigma$ are linked via Marcenko-Pastur.

nodes.name: Spectral decomposition of Xi tilde
nodes.statement:
We denote the spectral decomposition of matrix $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}$ by
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T - \tau, T} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where the eigenmatrix $\widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[1], \cdots, \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[p])$, whose $i$th column is the eigenvector of $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} $, and $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T - \tau, T} = \textrm{diag} \{ \widetilde{\lambda}_1 ,\cdots,  \widetilde{\lambda}_p\}$ is a diagonal matrix with non-increasing eigenvalues $\widetilde{\lambda}_1\geq \cdots \geq \widetilde{\lambda}_p$.

nodes.name: Oracle nonlinear shrinkage problem
nodes.statement:
The objective is to find the diagonal matrix ${\bf D}$ that solves the optimization problem
\[
\min\limits_{{\bf D} ~~\text{diag}}\| \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} {\bf D} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}} - \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\|_F.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Find the diagonal $D$ minimizing the Frobenius distance between $\widetilde U D\widetilde U^T$ and $\breve\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Oracle shrinkage solution
nodes.statement:
By elementary calculation, the solution is
\[D^{or} = \textrm{diag}(d_1^{or},\cdots, d_p^{or}),
\]
where
\begin{equation} d_i^{or} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i])^{{\mathrm{T}}} \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i].
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The optimal diagonal entries are $d_i^{or}=u_i^T\breve\Sigma u_i$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear shrinkage (NS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Therefore, we propose the following nonlinear shrinkage (NS) estimator for ICV:
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{NS}: = \hat{\theta}_p \cdot \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{NS},
\]
where $\widehat\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{NS} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} \textrm{diag}(\widehat{d_1^{or}},\cdots, \widehat{d_p^{or}}) \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau ,T}^{{\mathrm{T}}}$,
and $\widehat{d_i^{or}}$ is an estimator of $d_i^{or}$, solved by the algorithm proposed by \cite{LedoitandWolf2017}.
nodes.statement_short: NS estimator: $\hat\theta_p$ times $\widetilde U$ diag(estimated oracle $d_i^{or}$) $\widetilde U^T$, with $d_i^{or}$ estimated by Ledoit-Wolf's QuEST algorithm.

nodes.name: Oracle eigenvalue d_i^or
nodes.statement: d_i^{or} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i])^{{\mathrm{T}}} \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i].
nodes.label: eq: oracle di

nodes.name: Averaged nonlinear shrinkage (ANS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we have tick-by-tick high-frequency observations $\{{\bf Y}_{l_i}\}$ over time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$.
First, the estimator $\hat{\theta}_p = 3\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2/p$ can be established based on high-frequency data during time interval $[T - 1, T]$.
Suppose that there are in total $M_{\tau} = \tau \cdot M$ averaged noisy increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2j}, j = 1, \cdots, M_{\tau}$, over time period $[T - \tau, T]$, in which the overnight increments are excluded and there are $M$ increments each day.
Next, we permute the increments $B$ times.
At the $k$th permutation, we split the increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}$ into two parts, say $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)} = (\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_1, \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_2)$, for $k = 1,\cdots, B$, with $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_\ell$ having size $p\times M_{\tau_{\ell}}$ $(\ell = 1, 2)$ and $M_{\tau_1} + M_{\tau_2} = M_{\tau}$.
We define
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_{\ell}^{(k)} := \frac{p}{M_{\tau_{\ell}}}\sum_{i \in J_{\ell, k}}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2},
\]
where $J_{\ell, k} = \{i: \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} \in \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{\ell}^{(k)}\}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$ and $k = 1, \cdots, B$.
We denote the spectral decomposition of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)}$ as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_1^{(k)}(\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
for $k = 1,\cdots, B$.
Then the averaged nonlinear shrinkage (ANS) estimator of ICV is defined as
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\textrm{ANS}}:= \hat{\theta}_p\cdot\frac{1}{B} \sum_{k=1}^B \widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}}, ~~\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)} \textrm{diag}((\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}} \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_2^{(k)}\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}) (\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\end{equation*}
where $\textrm{diag}({\bf A})$ sets all non-diagonal elements of matrix ${\bf A}$ to zero.
To this end, $M_{\tau_1}$ is chosen using the following criterion,
\begin{equation}\arg\min\limits_{M_{\tau_1}\in \mathcal{G}} \bigg| \bigg|  \frac{1}{B} \sum_{k = 1}^B (\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}} -  \widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_2^{(k)}) \bigg| \bigg|_F^2, \end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{G} = \bigg[2M_{\tau}^{1/2}, 0.2M_{\tau}, 0.4M_{\tau},
0.6M_{\tau}, 0.8M_{\tau},
 M_{\tau} - 2.5M_{\tau}^{1/2}, M_{\tau} - 1.5M_{\tau}^{1/2}\bigg]
\end{split} \end{equation}
is the candidate set for $M_{\tau_1}$, recommended by \cite{Lam2016} and \cite{Lametal2017}.
input: tick-by-tick high-frequency observations $\{{\bf Y}_{l_i}\}$ over time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$
output: the averaged nonlinear shrinkage (ANS) estimator of ICV
nodes.statement_short: Data-splitting nonlinear shrinkage: over $B$ random permutations, rotate one split's eigenvectors and take eigenvalues from the other split, average, and rescale by $\hat\theta_p$. The split size is chosen from a candidate grid by a Frobenius criterion.

nodes.name: Split-size selection criterion
nodes.statement: \arg\min\limits_{M_{\tau_1}\in \mathcal{G}} \bigg| \bigg|  \frac{1}{B} \sum_{k = 1}^B (\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}} -  \widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_2^{(k)}) \bigg| \bigg|_F^2,
nodes.label: eq: nonlinear shrnkage criterion

nodes.name: Mixed nonlinear shrinkage (MNS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we observe high-frequency data $\{{\bf Y}_t\}$ with multiple transactions during time period $[T - \tau, T]$.
First, the matrix $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T-1}$ in \eqref{eq: definition of hbSigma} is constructed based on high-frequency data during time period $[T - \tau, T - 1]$, and its spectral decomposition is denoted as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T-\tau, T - 1}(\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where
\[
\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[1], \cdots, \widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[p]).
\]
Second, we set the eigenvectors $\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[k]$, $k = 1,\cdots, p$, to be given beforehand, and transform the averaged high-frequency data $\{\overline{{\bf Y}}_i\}$ during time period $[T - 1, T]$.
That is, consider $\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[k])^{{\mathrm{T}}}\overline{{\bf Y}}_i$ as the transformed averaged observations at recording time $t_i \in [T - 1,T]$, for $k = 1,\cdots, p, i = 0,\cdots, n$.
Third, for each $k = 1,\cdots, p$, compute the averaging-pre-averaging estimator 
\[
\widehat{d_i^{\textrm{APA}}} = \frac{12}{k_n }\sum_{i = 0}^{n - k_n + 1}(\Delta_{i,k_n}^k\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} )^2 - \frac{6}{\vartheta^2 n} \sum_{i = 0}^{n-1} (\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + 1}^{**} - \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**})^2,
\]
where $k_n = \lfloor \vartheta n^{1/2}\rfloor,  \vartheta>0$ and $\Delta_{i,k_n}^k\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} = \sum_{j = 1}^{k_n -1} g(j/k_n)( \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + j + 1}^{**} - \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + j}^{**})$ with $g(x) = x\wedge (1-x)$, which is a consistent estimator of the integrated volatility of $(\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**})$ over $[T - 1, T]$ by given ${\bf U}_{T - \tau, T - 1}$, see \cite{Jacodetal2009} and \cite{Liuetal2018}.
Finally, our mixed nonlinear shrinkage (MNS) estimator of ICV is defined as
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\textrm{MNS}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1} \textrm{diag} (\widehat{d_1^{\textrm{APA}}}, \cdots, \widehat{d_p^{\textrm{APA}}})\widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1}^{{\mathrm{T}}}.
\]
input: high-frequency data $\{{\bf Y}_t\}$ with multiple transactions during time period $[T - \tau, T]$
output: our mixed nonlinear shrinkage (MNS) estimator of ICV

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.1
nodes.statement:
\noindent\emph{Proof of Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma}.}  Recall that
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i} =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\Delta_{2i,j}{\bf X} +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\Delta_{2i-1,j}{\bf X},\]
where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i},  b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf X} = {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j - 1}$.
Then we separate $\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}$ into two parts,
\begin{equation}
\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i} = \sqrt{w_i}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_{i} + {\bf V}_i), \end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
w_i = \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt, \end{equation}
\[{\bf Z}_i =  \frac{1}{\sqrt{w_i}}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j} }\gamma_td{\bf W}_t +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-2} + j} }\gamma_td{\bf W}_t \right],\]
and
\[{\bf V}_i =  \frac{1}{\sqrt{w_i}}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j} }\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-2} + j} }\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt  \right].\]
Using the above notation, $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ can be rewritten as
\[\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \frac{({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)^{\mathrm{T}} }{|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2}.\]
Notice that
\[
\frac{1}{L_{2i}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}} a_{2i,j} = \frac{1}{2}(1 + \frac{1}{L_{2i}}), ~~ \frac{1}{L_{2i - 1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i - 1}} b_{2i-1, j} = \frac{1}{2}(1 - \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}})
\]
and
\[
\frac{1}{L_{2i}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}} a_{2i,j}^2  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6L_{2i}^2} + \frac{1}{2L_{2i}}, ~\frac{1}{L_{2i - 1}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i - 1}} b_{2i - 1,j}^2  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6L_{2i - 1}^2} - \frac{1}{2L_{2i-1}},
\]
which are all uniformly bounded as $L_i \geq 1$.
By the boundedness of $|\mu_t^{(l)}|$ and $|\gamma_t|$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu} and \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma}, and the equally spaced transaction durations $\Delta s_{i,j}$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}, there exists $C>0$ such that $|{\bf V}_i^{(l)}|\leq C/\sqrt{N}$ for all $i=1,\cdots,N,l=1,\cdots, p$, which indicates that the $|{\bf V}_i|$ are uniformly bounded.
By a similar argument to that used in (3.34) in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we have
\begin{equation}
\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq N} \big|\frac{1}{p}|\boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2-1\big| \to 0, \hspace{0.5cm} \text{almost surely}. \end{equation}
By the boundedness of the $|{\bf V}_i|$, we further have
\begin{equation}
\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq N} \big|\frac{1}{p}|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2-1\big| \to 0, \hspace{0.5cm} \text{almost surely}. \end{equation}
By the same arguments used in the proof of Theorem 2 in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we can show that Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.2
nodes.statement:
\noindent\emph{Proof of Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of wi}.} The convergence of $F^{ICV}$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:LSD_bH} and the fact that
\[F^{\textrm{ICV}}(x) = F^{\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}}\left(\frac{x}{\int_0^1\gamma_t^2dt}\right) \hspace{0.5cm} \text{for all~} x\geq 0.\]
We proceed to show the convergence of $1/p\cdot \sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2$.
Write $\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i} = \sqrt{w_i}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i + {\bf V}_i)$ as in \eqref{eq: expression of delta wbx}; then
\[
\dfrac 1p |\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2 = \dfrac 1p \sum_{i=1}^N w_i |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 =\sum_{i=1}^N Ew_i + \sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - Ew_i) + \varepsilon,
\]
where $\varepsilon = \sum_{i = 1}^N w_i (p^{-1} |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 - 1)$.
First, almost surely, that $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$ is bounded follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}.
Thus, combining this with the convergence of \eqref{eq: order of v pluz z}, the error term $\varepsilon$ converges to 0 almost surely.
Besides, $\sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - E(w_i))$ converges to zero almost surely by the Kolmogorov strong law of large numbers and the boundedness of $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$.
Next, we show that there exists a piecewise continuous process $(w_s)$ with finite jumps such that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^N \int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds =0,
\]
where $w_s = (\dfrac 13 + \dfrac 16 f_{2,s}^*)\cdot (\gamma_s^*)^2$.
Suppose that $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$, and $(f_{2,s}^*)$ have a finite number of jumps J in total. 
For each $j = 1,\cdots, J$, there exists an $\ell_j$ such that the $j$th jump falls in the interval $((2\ell_j - 2)/n, 2\ell_j/n]$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\sum_{i=1}^N\int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{\ell_j \in \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2\ell_j-2}{n}}^{\frac{2\ell_j}{n}}|N E(w_{\ell_j}) - w_s|ds +
\sum\limits_{i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
:= &D_1 + D_2.\\
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have
\[|D_1|\leq \frac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\]
Notice that
\[
E \left(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 \right)= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}^2}\big) + \frac{1}{2}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\big),
\]
and
\[ E\left( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1
,j}^2 \right)  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2}\big) - \frac{1}{2} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\big).
\]
For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$,  and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$,  and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$,  and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively.
For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have
\[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{for all}  ~~t \in [\frac{2i-2}{n},\frac{2i}{n} ],\]
for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.
Define
\[
\begin{split}
w_i^* &= \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt,\\
\widetilde{w}_i^*&= (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 + (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\\
\text{and}~~~
 \widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*&=(\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2\cdot\frac{2}{n}\bigg(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}f_{2, 2i/n}^*\bigg).
\end{split}
\]
For all large $n$, because $|\gamma_t|\leq C$ and $1\leq L_i< L^*$, for any $i, t$, we have
\[
\begin{split}
&|D_2| \\
\leq& \sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N|E(w_i) - E(w_i^*)|ds + \sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N| E(w_i^*) - E(\widetilde{w}_i^*)|ds \\
+&\sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| NE(\widetilde{w}_i^*) - N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*|ds  +\sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^* - w_s|ds\\
\to& 0, ~~~\text{almost surely.}
\end{split}
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of Vi plus lambda Zi}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.1
nodes.statement:
\noindent\emph{Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:LSD ttSigma}.}
To prove the convergence of $F^{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}}$, we shall show that
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} = \frac{p}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}(\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2}~~~\text{and}~~~
\widetilde{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}} := \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD.
Following the same arguments as in the proof of Proposition C.1 of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}, it suffices to show that
\begin{equation}
\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \frac{\sqrt{p}|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{(j)}|}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|}\to 0,\hspace{1cm} \text{almost surely}. \end{equation}
We start by showing that there exists a constant $\widetilde{C}>0$ for large $M$, such that
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 \geq \widetilde{C}.
\end{equation}


By equation \eqref{eqn:Delta_V}, we decompose $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}= & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left(\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h + j} - \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left( \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j} -  \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) \notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left (1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+l}\notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}a_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l|}{h} \right )\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}.\\
\end{align*}
From the fact that  $a_{i,j} + b_{i,j} = 1$, we can further write $ \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as

\begin{align} \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i} = & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\Delta_{2ih,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right)\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
:= & \widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i,
\end{align}
where
\begin{align*}
\psi_i &:= \frac{1}{h^2}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right]^2\\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}} \gamma_t^2dt,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i& := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\psi_i}}\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\gamma_td{\bf W}_t\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right] \\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}} \gamma_td{\bf W}_t,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i &:= \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right] \\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}}\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt.
\end{align*}
Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\gamma_t$ and ${\bf W}_t$ are independent, which leads to the fact that each entry of $\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i$ is i.i.d. standard normal.
Otherwise, by using a similar trick as in the proof of (3.34) of \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we have
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\frac{1}{p}|\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2  - 1 | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
Combining this with the fact that all the entries of $\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i$ are of order $O(h/n) = o(1/\sqrt{p})$, we have
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2}{p} = \sum_{i=1}^M\psi_i + o_{a.s.}(1). \end{equation}

Thus, from equation \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX},  we have
\[
|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 = |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i|^2 + |\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 - 2|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| | \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|.
\]
Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma} implies that for all $i$, there exists $C'$ such that$|\psi_i|\geq C'h/n.$
Taking this together with Assumption \eqref{asm:dim_windows} and Equation \eqref{eq: norm convergeb=nce of tbZ}, there exists $C^*>0$ such that for all $n$ large enough,
\[
\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq m}|\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq C^*.
\]
Moreover, $\max_i |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| =O(\sqrt{p}\times h/n) = o(1)$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}.
Therefore \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX} follows.
Next, we will show that
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~ \text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
Observe that $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)}) = (1/L_i\sum_{k=1}^{L_i}\varepsilon_{i,k}^{(j)})$ is also a $\rho$-mixing sequence following from Definition \ref{def: rho-misiing}, and the $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\bar{\rho}^j(r)$ based on $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)})$ have the same order as $\rho^j(r)$ by the boundedness of $L_i$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_L}.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} follows by the same process used in (C.7) of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}, which, together with \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}, implies that \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing noise is negligible relative to latent returns: bound $|\Delta\widetilde{\overline X}_{2i}|^2$ below via a decomposition into a Gaussian part and drift, and bound noise via rho-mixing.
