nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \frac{\sqrt{p}|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{(j)}|}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|}\to 0,\hspace{1cm} \text{almost surely}.
nodes.label: eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x

nodes.name: Lower bound on pre-averaged returns
nodes.statement: \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 \geq \widetilde{C}.
nodes.label: eq: minimun of twbX

nodes.name: Decomposition of pre-averaged latent return
nodes.statement:
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i} = & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\Delta_{2ih,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right)\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
:= & \widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i,
nodes.label: eq: expression for tbwX

nodes.name: Norm concentration of Lambda Z tilde
nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\frac{1}{p}|\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2  - 1 | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely}.
nodes.label: eq: norm convergeb=nce of tbZ

nodes.name: Scale term equals sum of psi_i
nodes.statement: \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2}{p} = \sum_{i=1}^M\psi_i + o_{a.s.}(1).
nodes.label: eq: psii plus error term

nodes.name: Uniform smallness of pre-averaged noise
nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~ \text{almost surely}.
nodes.label: eq: sqrtt p delta twbe

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.2
nodes.statement:
\noindent\emph{Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:theta estimation}.}
Note that
\[\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 + 2\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i} + \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2.
\]
The convergence of \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2/p \to 0$ almost surely.
It remains to prove that
\begin{equation} \lim_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = \theta, \hspace{1cm} \text{almost surely},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}}{p}\to 0, \hspace{1cm}\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
To show \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, by \eqref{eq: psii plus error term}, it suffices to show that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds =0,
\]
almost surely.
Suppose that  $\gamma_t^*$ has $J$ jumps at $\{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}$; then
\begin{align*}
&\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{i \in \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
&+ \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
:= &\Delta_1 + \Delta_2.
\end{align*}
For any $\epsilon > 0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, $|\Delta_1| \leq \epsilon$ follows from the boundedness of $|M\psi_i|$ and $\gamma_t^*$.
For the second term, $\Delta_2$, by defining $\psi_i^*$ by replacing $\gamma_t$ with $\gamma_t^*$ from the definition of $\psi_i$, we have
\[
|\Delta_2| \leq \Delta_{21} + \Delta_{22} + \Delta_{23} +\Delta_{24},
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
\Delta_{21} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - M\psi_i^*|ds,\\
\Delta_{22} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M\psi_i^* - M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i|ds,\\
\Delta_{23} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i - M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i |ds,\\
\Delta_{24} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_{s}^*)^2 |ds,
\end{split}
\]
and
\[
\begin{split}
A_i := &\frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} + \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Big[1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h}+ \\
&\hspace{1cm}+\frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \Big]^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} .
\end{split}
\]
We further decompose $A_i$ as $A_i = A_{i1} +  A_{i2} + A_{i3}+ A_{i4}$, where
\begin{align*}
A_{i1} &:= \frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),\\
A_{i2} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)^2\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j}= \frac{2h}{3n} + o(\frac{h}{n}),\\
A_{i3} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{2}{h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)(|h-l+1| - |h-l|) \\
&\cdot b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} = O(\frac{1}{n}),\\
A_{i4} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{1}{h^2}(|h-l+1| - |h-l|)^2b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \\
&= O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\end{align*}
follow from the boundedness of $L_i$ both below and above, and $\Delta s_{i,j} = O(1/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:interval}.
As $(\gamma_t^*)$ is continuous in $[s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}, s_{T_{2ih}}]$ when $i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}$, $(\gamma_t)$ uniformly converges to $(\gamma_t^*)$  by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma}, and $\psi_i^* = O(h/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_L}, for any $\epsilon >0 $ and sufficiently large $n,p$, it is easy to show that
\[
|MA_i - 1/3|\leq \epsilon ~~~\text{and}~~~\max\{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{22}, \Delta_{23},\Delta_{24}  \}<C\epsilon.
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}.
Finally, \eqref{eq: twbX plus twbe} follows from \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx} and \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Expand the noisy sum of squares; noise and cross terms vanish, and $3\sum|\Delta\widetilde{\overline X}_{2i}|^2/p\to\theta$ via approximating $M\psi_i$ by $(\gamma_s^*)^2/3$.

nodes.name: Latent pre-averaged scale converges to theta
nodes.statement: \lim_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = \theta, \hspace{1cm} \text{almost surely},
nodes.label: eq: convergence of sum of TWBx

nodes.name: Cross term vanishes
nodes.statement: \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}}{p}\to 0, \hspace{1cm}\text{almost surely}.
nodes.label: eq: twbX plus twbe

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
Without of generality, we may assume that  $\gamma_t$ is independent of ${\bf W}_t$.
Suppose that we have $L_i^{(q)}(\geq 1)$ observations for each stock $q$ at recording time $t_i = i/n$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots, p$ and $i = 1,2,\cdots, n$.
Recall that for any process $({\bf V}_t)$, $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ denote the observation of the $j$th transaction for stock $q$ during time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$,
and the true transaction time of $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ is denoted as $s_{T_{i-1}+j}^{(q)}$, for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i^{(q)}$ satisfying $t_{i-1} \leq s_{T_{i-1}}^{(q)}< s_{T_{i-1} + 1}^{(q)}<\cdots < s_{T_{i-1} + L_i^{(q)}}^{(q)} = s_{T_i}^{(q)} \leq t_i$.
Under asynchronous trading conditions, the average of multiple observations at each recording time $t_i$ is denoted by
\[
\overline{\bf{V}}^*_i := \left(\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(1)}}V_{i,j}^{(1)}, \cdots, \sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(p)}}V_{i,j}^{(p)} \right)^{{\mathrm{T}}};
\]
thus, the increment at trading time $t_i$ becomes
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf V}}^*_i :=  \begin{pmatrix}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}a_{i,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(1)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(1)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(1)}V\\
\vdots\\
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}a_{i,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(p)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(p)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(p)}V\\
\end{pmatrix},\]
where $a_{i,j}^{(q)} = 1 - \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$, $b_{i,j}^{(q)} =  \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$ and  $\Delta_{i,j}^{(q)}X = X_{i, j}^{(q)} -  X_{i, j-1}^{(q)}$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots,p$.
Similar to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:LSD ttSigma}, we first show that
there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for large $M$
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i\leq M} |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}|^2 \geq C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta (\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{*})^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely,}
\end{equation}
which leads to the result that the PA-ATVA matrix based on noisy observations $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^*_{2i}$ and that based on latent log price $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}$ have the same LSD.
We only need to prove \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT}, as \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT done} holds straightforwardly from the proof of \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} given earlier.
By a similar decomposition to that used in \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX}, the return based on the pre-averaged (latent) price can be decomposed as
\[
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^* = \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h+j}^* - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j}^* = {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf M}_{i} + {\bf R}_{i2},
\]
where ${\bf M}_i = (M_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, M_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i\ell} = (R_{i\ell}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i\ell}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$, and their $q$th components have the form
\begin{align*}
R_{i1}^{(q)} = &\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}^{(q)}}a_{2ih,j}^{(q)}\Delta_{2ih,j}^{(q)}X,\\
M_{i}^{(q)} = & \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}^{(q)} }c_{l,h} \Delta_{(2i-2)h + l,j}^{(q)}X,\\
R_{i2}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}^{(q)}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}
b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)} X,
\end{align*}
where $c_{l,h} = 1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} $.
Note that $M_i^{(q)}$ can be reduced to
\[
\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \cdot (X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1} }^{(q)}}^{(q)}).
\]
We further decompose $M_i^{(q)}$ as $W_i^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$, where
\begin{align*}
W_{i}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} (X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l}}^{(q)} -  X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}),\\
R_{i3}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \left(  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)} + X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l -1}}^{(q)} -  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}}^{(q)}  \right),
\end{align*}
and $X_{t_i}^{(q)}$ denotes the log price for stock $q$ at recording time $t_i$.  Let ${\bf W}_i = (W_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, W_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i3} = (R_{i3}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i3}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$.
Thus, $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^*  = {\bf W}_i + {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf R}_{i2}  + {\bf R}_{i3} $.
As 
\[{\bf W}_{i} = \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) \Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^*,
\]
and 
\[
\Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^* = \begin{pmatrix}
X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(1)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(1)}\\
 \vdots\\
  X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(p)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(p)}\\
  \end{pmatrix},
\]
it reduces to the synchronous setting.
Using a similar argument to that in \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, we have
\[ \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
Thus, \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT} follows if we can show that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for large $M$
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M}|{\bf W}_{i}|^2\geq C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq q \leq p}\sqrt{p}|R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} +  R_{i3}^{(q)}|\to 0,~~~\text{almost surely.}
\end{equation}
Hence, the PA-ATVA matrix based on noisy observations $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^*_{2i}$ and that based on latent log price $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}$ have the same LSD.
Further, using \eqref{eq: min of Wi2}, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, and Lemma \ref{lem: appendix B lemma 1}, we obtain that
\[
3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p} \cdot \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^* (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}
~~\text{and}~~3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD, and
\[
\lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p}=  \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
Moreover, the LSD of  $3 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_{i}|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}$ is generated by Theorem 2.3 of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}.
Therefore, the proof of Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA asynt} is complete.

Finally, we only need to show the proofs of \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} and \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}.
Notice that \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} follows naturally from the proof of \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}.
To prove \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, by the normality of $R_{i1}^{(q)}$, $R_{i2}^{(q)}$, and $R_{i3}^{(q)}$, Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}, and $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n, 1\leq q\leq  p} nh(s_{T_i}^{(q)} - t_i) \to 0 $ almost surely, we have
\[
E(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),
\]
\[E(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\]
and
\[E(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}).
\]
Let $R_{i}^{(q)} = R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$; thus, by $C_p$ inequality and the normality of $R_{i}^{(q)} $, we have for any $\kappa\geq 1$, 
\[
 E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) < Cn^{-1} ~~\text{and}~~ E|R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa} \leq Cn^{-\kappa},
\]
for all $i, q$.
Hence,  it follows that for any $\varepsilon >0$ and $\kappa \geq 1$,
\[
\begin{split}
&P\left(\max\limits_{i,q} \sqrt{p}| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |\geq \varepsilon\right) \\
&\leq \sum\limits_{i,q}\frac{p^{\kappa} E| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}}\\
&\leq C\cdot \frac{Mp\cdot p^{\kappa} \cdot n^{-\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}} = O(p^{2-\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)}).
\end{split}
\]
We choose $\kappa$ large enough such that $\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)- 2 > 1$.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key} holds by the Borel--Cantelli lemma.
\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the asynchronous pre-averaged return to the synchronous one plus remainders, show remainders vanish uniformly by moment bounds and Borel-Cantelli, and conclude with Lemma D.1 and Xia-Zheng Theorem 2.3.

nodes.name: Lower bound on asynchronous pre-averaged returns
nodes.statement: \min\limits_{1\leq i\leq M} |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}|^2 \geq C,
nodes.label: eq: xy same require in AT

nodes.name: Asynchronous noise uniformly small
nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta (\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{*})^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely,}
nodes.label: eq: xy same require in AT done

nodes.name: Lower bound on synchronous part W_i
nodes.statement: \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M}|{\bf W}_{i}|^2\geq C,
nodes.label: eq: min of Wi2

nodes.name: Asynchronous remainders uniformly small
nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq q \leq p}\sqrt{p}|R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} +  R_{i3}^{(q)}|\to 0,~~~\text{almost surely.}
nodes.label: eq: asynchronous key

nodes.name: Perturbation lemma for LSD (Zheng and Li, Lemma 1)
assumptions: there exists a sequence $\epsilon_p = o(1/\sqrt{p})$ such that for all $p$ and all $l$, all the entries of $\bm v_l$ are bounded by $\epsilon_p$ in absolute value;
nodes.statement_short: Small uniform perturbations ($o(1/\sqrt p)$ entries) of the vectors do not change the LSD of a sum of outer products.
nodes.label: lem: appendix B lemma 1

nodes.name: Recall averaged return form
nodes.statement:
Recall that
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i} =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\Delta_{2i,j}{\bf X} +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\Delta_{2i-1,j}{\bf X},\]
where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i},  b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf X} = {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j - 1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the weighted-sum form of $\Delta\overline X_{2i}$.

nodes.name: Split into Gaussian and drift parts
nodes.statement_short: Write $\Delta\overline X_{2i}=\sqrt{w_i}(\Lambda Z_i+V_i)$, defining $w_i$, $Z_i$, $V_i$.

nodes.name: Rewrite Sigma tilde
nodes.statement:
Using the above notation, $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ can be rewritten as
\[\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \frac{({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)^{\mathrm{T}} }{|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Express $\widetilde\Sigma$ via $V_i+\Lambda Z_i$.

nodes.name: Weight sums are bounded
nodes.statement_short: Compute averages of $a_{i,j}$, $b_{i,j}$ and their squares; all bounded.

nodes.name: Drift part is uniformly small
nodes.statement: By the boundedness of $|\mu_t^{(l)}|$ and $|\gamma_t|$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu} and \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma}, and the equally spaced transaction durations $\Delta s_{i,j}$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}, there exists $C>0$ such that $|{\bf V}_i^{(l)}|\leq C/\sqrt{N}$ for all $i=1,\cdots,N,l=1,\cdots, p$, which indicates that the $|{\bf V}_i|$ are uniformly bounded.
nodes.statement_short: Assumptions give $|V_i^{(l)}|\le C/\sqrt N$, so $|V_i|$ is bounded.

nodes.name: Norm concentration of Lambda Z_i
nodes.statement_short: As in Zheng and Li (3.34), $|\Lambda Z_i|^2/p\to1$ uniformly.

nodes.name: Norm concentration with drift
nodes.statement_short: Extend concentration to $V_i+\Lambda Z_i$.

nodes.name: Conclude via Zheng-Li argument
nodes.statement: By the same arguments used in the proof of Theorem 2 in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we can show that Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Finish as in Zheng and Li's Theorem 2.

nodes.name: LSD of ICV
nodes.statement:
The convergence of $F^{ICV}$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:LSD_bH} and the fact that
\[F^{\textrm{ICV}}(x) = F^{\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}}\left(\frac{x}{\int_0^1\gamma_t^2dt}\right) \hspace{0.5cm} \text{for all~} x\geq 0.\]
nodes.statement_short: ICV's ESD is a rescaling of $\breve\Sigma$'s, so it converges by the LSD assumption.

nodes.name: Turn to the scale term
nodes.statement: We proceed to show the convergence of $1/p\cdot \sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Next show convergence of $\sum|\Delta\overline X_{2i}|^2/p$.

nodes.name: Decompose scale term
nodes.statement:
Write $\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i} = \sqrt{w_i}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i + {\bf V}_i)$ as in \eqref{eq: expression of delta wbx}; then
\[
\dfrac 1p |\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2 = \dfrac 1p \sum_{i=1}^N w_i |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 =\sum_{i=1}^N Ew_i + \sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - Ew_i) + \varepsilon,
\]
where $\varepsilon = \sum_{i = 1}^N w_i (p^{-1} |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 - 1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Split into $\sum E w_i$, centered part and error $\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Bound N w_i
nodes.statement: First, almost surely, that $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$ is bounded follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}.
nodes.statement_short: $N w_i$ is uniformly bounded by the assumptions.

nodes.name: Error term vanishes
nodes.statement: Thus, combining this with the convergence of \eqref{eq: order of v pluz z}, the error term $\varepsilon$ converges to 0 almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: With norm concentration, $\varepsilon\to0$ a.s.

nodes.name: Strong law for centered part
nodes.statement: Besides, $\sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - E(w_i))$ converges to zero almost surely by the Kolmogorov strong law of large numbers and the boundedness of $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Kolmogorov's strong law kills the centered part.

nodes.name: Mean term approximates integral
nodes.statement:
Next, we show that there exists a piecewise continuous process $(w_s)$ with finite jumps such that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^N \int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds =0,
\]
where $w_s = (\dfrac 13 + \dfrac 16 f_{2,s}^*)\cdot (\gamma_s^*)^2$.
Suppose that $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$, and $(f_{2,s}^*)$ have a finite number of jumps J in total. 
For each $j = 1,\cdots, J$, there exists an $\ell_j$ such that the $j$th jump falls in the interval $((2\ell_j - 2)/n, 2\ell_j/n]$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\sum_{i=1}^N\int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{\ell_j \in \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2\ell_j-2}{n}}^{\frac{2\ell_j}{n}}|N E(w_{\ell_j}) - w_s|ds +
\sum\limits_{i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
:= &D_1 + D_2.\\
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have
\[|D_1|\leq \frac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\]
Notice that
\[
E \left(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 \right)= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}^2}\big) + \frac{1}{2}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\big),
\]
and
\[ E\left( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1
,j}^2 \right)  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2}\big) - \frac{1}{2} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\big).
\]
For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$,  and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$,  and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$,  and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively.
For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have
\[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{for all}  ~~t \in [\frac{2i-2}{n},\frac{2i}{n} ],\]
for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.
Define
\[
\begin{split}
w_i^* &= \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt,\\
\widetilde{w}_i^*&= (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 + (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\\
\text{and}~~~
 \widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*&=(\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2\cdot\frac{2}{n}\bigg(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}f_{2, 2i/n}^*\bigg).
\end{split}
\]
For all large $n$, because $|\gamma_t|\leq C$ and $1\leq L_i< L^*$, for any $i, t$, we have
\[
\begin{split}
&|D_2| \\
\leq& \sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N|E(w_i) - E(w_i^*)|ds + \sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N| E(w_i^*) - E(\widetilde{w}_i^*)|ds \\
+&\sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| NE(\widetilde{w}_i^*) - N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*|ds  +\sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^* - w_s|ds\\
\to& 0, ~~~\text{almost surely.}
\end{split}
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of Vi plus lambda Zi}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Show $N E(w_i)$ approximates $w_s=(1/3+f_{2,s}^*/6)(\gamma_s^*)^2$ in $L^1$.

nodes.name: Locate the jumps
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$, and $(f_{2,s}^*)$ have a finite number of jumps J in total. 
For each $j = 1,\cdots, J$, there exists an $\ell_j$ such that the $j$th jump falls in the interval $((2\ell_j - 2)/n, 2\ell_j/n]$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $J$ jumps fall in intervals indexed by $\ell_j$.

nodes.name: Split into D1 and D2
nodes.statement_short: Split the error into jump intervals $D_1$ and the rest $D_2$.

nodes.name: Bound D1
nodes.statement:
As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have
\[|D_1|\leq \frac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\]

nodes.name: Expected weight sums
nodes.statement:
Notice that
\[
E \left(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 \right)= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}^2}\big) + \frac{1}{2}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\big),
\]
and
\[ E\left( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1
,j}^2 \right)  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2}\big) - \frac{1}{2} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Expectations of the squared-weight averages in terms of $f_1,f_2$.

nodes.name: Continuity on non-jump intervals
nodes.statement: For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$,  and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$,  and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$,  and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Off jumps the limits are continuous and the convergence uniform.

nodes.name: Uniform closeness
nodes.statement:
For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have
\[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{for all}  ~~t \in [\frac{2i-2}{n},\frac{2i}{n} ],\]
for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Local closeness of $\gamma$ and $f_2$ to their limits.

nodes.name: Intermediate approximations
nodes.statement_short: Define $w_i^*$, $\widetilde w_i^*$, $\widetilde{\widetilde w}_i^*$.

nodes.name: Bound D2 by telescoping
nodes.statement_short: Telescoping through the intermediate approximations gives $D_2\to0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to noise-free matrix
nodes.statement:
To prove the convergence of $F^{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}}$, we shall show that
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} = \frac{p}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}(\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2}~~~\text{and}~~~
\widetilde{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}} := \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD.
nodes.statement_short: Show the noisy and latent self-normalized matrices share an LSD.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: noise is uniformly negligible relative to latent returns.

nodes.name: Lower bound on latent returns
nodes.statement:
We start by showing that there exists a constant $\widetilde{C}>0$ for large $M$, such that
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 \geq \widetilde{C}.
\end{equation}


By equation \eqref{eqn:Delta_V}, we decompose $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}= & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left(\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h + j} - \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left( \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j} -  \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) \notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left (1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+l}\notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}a_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l|}{h} \right )\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}.\\
\end{align*}
From the fact that  $a_{i,j} + b_{i,j} = 1$, we can further write $ \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as

\begin{align} \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i} = & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\Delta_{2ih,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right)\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
&+ \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X} \notag\\
:= & \widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i,
\end{align}
where
\begin{align*}
\psi_i &:= \frac{1}{h^2}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right]^2\\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}} \gamma_t^2dt,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i& := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\psi_i}}\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\gamma_td{\bf W}_t\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right] \\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}} \gamma_td{\bf W}_t,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i &:= \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}}a_{2ih,j}\int_{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{2ih-1} + j}}\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}} \left[\left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) + \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h} b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\right] \\
&\hspace{2cm}\cdot\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j - 1}}^{s_{T_{(2i-2)h+l-1} + j}}\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt.
\end{align*}
Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\gamma_t$ and ${\bf W}_t$ are independent, which leads to the fact that each entry of $\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i$ is i.i.d. standard normal.
Otherwise, by using a similar trick as in the proof of (3.34) of \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we have
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M} |\frac{1}{p}|\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2  - 1 | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
Combining this with the fact that all the entries of $\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i$ are of order $O(h/n) = o(1/\sqrt{p})$, we have
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2}{p} = \sum_{i=1}^M\psi_i + o_{a.s.}(1). \end{equation}

Thus, from equation \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX},  we have
\[
|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 = |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i|^2 + |\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 - 2|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| | \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|.
\]
Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma} implies that for all $i$, there exists $C'$ such that$|\psi_i|\geq C'h/n.$
Taking this together with Assumption \eqref{asm:dim_windows} and Equation \eqref{eq: norm convergeb=nce of tbZ}, there exists $C^*>0$ such that for all $n$ large enough,
\[
\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq m}|\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq C^*.
\]
Moreover, $\max_i |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| =O(\sqrt{p}\times h/n) = o(1)$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}.
Therefore \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\min_i|\Delta\widetilde{\overline X}_{2i}|^2\ge\widetilde C$.

nodes.name: Noise is uniformly small
nodes.statement:
Next, we will show that
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~ \text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
Observe that $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)}) = (1/L_i\sum_{k=1}^{L_i}\varepsilon_{i,k}^{(j)})$ is also a $\rho$-mixing sequence following from Definition \ref{def: rho-misiing}, and the $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\bar{\rho}^j(r)$ based on $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)})$ have the same order as $\rho^j(r)$ by the boundedness of $L_i$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_L}.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} follows by the same process used in (C.7) of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}, which, together with \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}, implies that \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Show $\max\sqrt p|\Delta\widetilde{\overline\varepsilon}_{2i}^{(j)}|\to0$.

nodes.name: Expand pre-averaged return
nodes.statement:
By equation \eqref{eqn:Delta_V}, we decompose $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}= & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left(\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h + j} - \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left( \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j} -  \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) \notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left (1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+l}\notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}a_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l|}{h} \right )\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}.\\
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the pre-averaged return as a triangular-kernel sum of tick returns.

nodes.name: Gaussian plus drift form
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite as $\widetilde V_i+\sqrt{\psi_i}\Lambda\widetilde Z_i$.

nodes.name: Independence WLOG
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\gamma_t$ and ${\bf W}_t$ are independent, which leads to the fact that each entry of $\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i$ is i.i.d. standard normal.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $\gamma$ independent of $W$, making $\widetilde Z_i$ standard normal.

nodes.name: Norm concentration of Z tilde
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise use Zheng-Li's trick for norm concentration.

nodes.name: Scale term equals sum psi_i
nodes.statement_short: Drift is $o(1/\sqrt p)$, so the scale term is $\sum\psi_i+o(1)$.

nodes.name: Triangle lower bound
nodes.statement:
Thus, from equation \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX},  we have
\[
|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 = |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i|^2 + |\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 - 2|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| | \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound $|\Delta\widetilde{\overline X}_{2i}|^2$ by the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Lower bound on psi_i
nodes.statement: Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma} implies that for all $i$, there exists $C'$ such that$|\psi_i|\geq C'h/n.$
nodes.statement_short: $|\psi_i|\ge C'h/n$.

nodes.name: Gaussian part bounded below
nodes.statement:
Taking this together with Assumption \eqref{asm:dim_windows} and Equation \eqref{eq: norm convergeb=nce of tbZ}, there exists $C^*>0$ such that for all $n$ large enough,
\[
\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq m}|\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq C^*.
\]
nodes.statement_short: $\min_i\psi_i|\Lambda\widetilde Z_i|^2\ge C^*$.

nodes.name: Drift negligible
nodes.statement: Moreover, $\max_i |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| =O(\sqrt{p}\times h/n) = o(1)$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}.
nodes.statement_short: $\max_i|\widetilde V_i|=o(1)$.

nodes.name: Lower bound established
nodes.statement: Therefore \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the lower bound.

nodes.name: Averaged noise is rho-mixing
nodes.statement: Observe that $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)}) = (1/L_i\sum_{k=1}^{L_i}\varepsilon_{i,k}^{(j)})$ is also a $\rho$-mixing sequence following from Definition \ref{def: rho-misiing}, and the $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\bar{\rho}^j(r)$ based on $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)})$ have the same order as $\rho^j(r)$ by the boundedness of $L_i$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_L}.
nodes.statement_short: Averaged noise stays $\rho$-mixing with the same coefficient order.

nodes.name: Conclude via Xia-Zheng
nodes.statement: Therefore, \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} follows by the same process used in (C.7) of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}, which, together with \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}, implies that \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Apply Xia-Zheng (C.7) and combine with the lower bound.

nodes.name: Expand noisy sum of squares
nodes.statement:
Note that
\[\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 + 2\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i} + \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Expand into latent, cross and noise terms.

nodes.name: Noise term vanishes
nodes.statement: The convergence of \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2/p \to 0$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Noise sum of squares over $p$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Remaining two limits
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the latent scale limit and the cross term.

nodes.name: Reduce to psi_i approximation
nodes.statement:
To show \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, by \eqref{eq: psii plus error term}, it suffices to show that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds =0,
\]
almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: $M\psi_i$ approximates $(\gamma_s^*)^2/3$ in $L^1$.

nodes.name: Split at jumps
nodes.statement:
Suppose that  $\gamma_t^*$ has $J$ jumps at $\{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}$; then
\begin{align*}
&\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{i \in \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
&+ \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
:= &\Delta_1 + \Delta_2.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split into jump intervals $\Delta_1$ and the rest $\Delta_2$.

nodes.name: Bound Delta1
nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon > 0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, $|\Delta_1| \leq \epsilon$ follows from the boundedness of $|M\psi_i|$ and $\gamma_t^*$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Delta_1$ is small by boundedness.

nodes.name: Decompose Delta2
nodes.statement:
For the second term, $\Delta_2$, by defining $\psi_i^*$ by replacing $\gamma_t$ with $\gamma_t^*$ from the definition of $\psi_i$, we have
\[
|\Delta_2| \leq \Delta_{21} + \Delta_{22} + \Delta_{23} +\Delta_{24},
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
\Delta_{21} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - M\psi_i^*|ds,\\
\Delta_{22} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M\psi_i^* - M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i|ds,\\
\Delta_{23} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i - M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i |ds,\\
\Delta_{24} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_{s}^*)^2 |ds,
\end{split}
\]
and
\[
\begin{split}
A_i := &\frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} + \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Big[1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h}+ \\
&\hspace{1cm}+\frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \Big]^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} .
\end{split}
\]
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Delta_2$ by four telescoping terms involving $A_i$.

nodes.name: Orders of A_i pieces
nodes.statement:
We further decompose $A_i$ as $A_i = A_{i1} +  A_{i2} + A_{i3}+ A_{i4}$, where
\begin{align*}
A_{i1} &:= \frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),\\
A_{i2} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)^2\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j}= \frac{2h}{3n} + o(\frac{h}{n}),\\
A_{i3} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{2}{h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)(|h-l+1| - |h-l|) \\
&\cdot b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} = O(\frac{1}{n}),\\
A_{i4} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{1}{h^2}(|h-l+1| - |h-l|)^2b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \\
&= O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\end{align*}
follow from the boundedness of $L_i$ both below and above, and $\Delta s_{i,j} = O(1/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:interval}.
nodes.statement_short: Only $A_{i2}=2h/(3n)$ is of leading order.

nodes.name: Bound the four terms
nodes.statement:
As $(\gamma_t^*)$ is continuous in $[s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}, s_{T_{2ih}}]$ when $i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}$, $(\gamma_t)$ uniformly converges to $(\gamma_t^*)$  by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma}, and $\psi_i^* = O(h/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_L}, for any $\epsilon >0 $ and sufficiently large $n,p$, it is easy to show that
\[
|MA_i - 1/3|\leq \epsilon ~~~\text{and}~~~\max\{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{22}, \Delta_{23},\Delta_{24}  \}<C\epsilon.
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}.
nodes.statement_short: $|MA_i-1/3|\le\epsilon$ and each $\Delta_{2k}<C\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Cross term vanishes
nodes.statement: Finally, \eqref{eq: twbX plus twbe} follows from \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx} and \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Cross term follows from the two previous limits.

nodes.name: Setup asynchronous notation
nodes.statement:
Without of generality, we may assume that  $\gamma_t$ is independent of ${\bf W}_t$.
Suppose that we have $L_i^{(q)}(\geq 1)$ observations for each stock $q$ at recording time $t_i = i/n$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots, p$ and $i = 1,2,\cdots, n$.
Recall that for any process $({\bf V}_t)$, $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ denote the observation of the $j$th transaction for stock $q$ during time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$,
and the true transaction time of $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ is denoted as $s_{T_{i-1}+j}^{(q)}$, for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i^{(q)}$ satisfying $t_{i-1} \leq s_{T_{i-1}}^{(q)}< s_{T_{i-1} + 1}^{(q)}<\cdots < s_{T_{i-1} + L_i^{(q)}}^{(q)} = s_{T_i}^{(q)} \leq t_i$.
Under asynchronous trading conditions, the average of multiple observations at each recording time $t_i$ is denoted by
\[
\overline{\bf{V}}^*_i := \left(\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(1)}}V_{i,j}^{(1)}, \cdots, \sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(p)}}V_{i,j}^{(p)} \right)^{{\mathrm{T}}};
\]
thus, the increment at trading time $t_i$ becomes
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf V}}^*_i :=  \begin{pmatrix}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}a_{i,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(1)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(1)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(1)}V\\
\vdots\\
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}a_{i,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(p)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(p)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(p)}V\\
\end{pmatrix},\]
where $a_{i,j}^{(q)} = 1 - \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$, $b_{i,j}^{(q)} =  \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$ and  $\Delta_{i,j}^{(q)}X = X_{i, j}^{(q)} -  X_{i, j-1}^{(q)}$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots,p$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume independence WLOG and recall the asynchronous averaged increments.

nodes.name: Two sufficient bounds
nodes.statement_short: As in Lemma B.1, need a lower bound on latent returns and uniformly small noise.

nodes.name: Noise bound already known
nodes.statement: We only need to prove \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT}, as \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT done} holds straightforwardly from the proof of \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} given earlier.
nodes.statement_short: The noise bound follows as in Lemma B.1.

nodes.name: Decompose asynchronous return
nodes.statement:
By a similar decomposition to that used in \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX}, the return based on the pre-averaged (latent) price can be decomposed as
\[
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^* = \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h+j}^* - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j}^* = {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf M}_{i} + {\bf R}_{i2},
\]
where ${\bf M}_i = (M_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, M_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i\ell} = (R_{i\ell}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i\ell}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$, and their $q$th components have the form
\begin{align*}
R_{i1}^{(q)} = &\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}^{(q)}}a_{2ih,j}^{(q)}\Delta_{2ih,j}^{(q)}X,\\
M_{i}^{(q)} = & \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}^{(q)} }c_{l,h} \Delta_{(2i-2)h + l,j}^{(q)}X,\\
R_{i2}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}^{(q)}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}
b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)} X,
\end{align*}
where $c_{l,h} = 1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} $.
nodes.statement_short: Write the return as $R_{i1}+M_i+R_{i2}$.

nodes.name: Synchronous part plus remainder
nodes.statement:
Note that $M_i^{(q)}$ can be reduced to
\[
\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \cdot (X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1} }^{(q)}}^{(q)}).
\]
We further decompose $M_i^{(q)}$ as $W_i^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$, where
\begin{align*}
W_{i}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} (X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l}}^{(q)} -  X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}),\\
R_{i3}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \left(  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)} + X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l -1}}^{(q)} -  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}}^{(q)}  \right),
\end{align*}
and $X_{t_i}^{(q)}$ denotes the log price for stock $q$ at recording time $t_i$.  Let ${\bf W}_i = (W_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, W_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i3} = (R_{i3}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i3}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$.
Thus, $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^*  = {\bf W}_i + {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf R}_{i2}  + {\bf R}_{i3} $.
nodes.statement_short: Split $M_i=W_i+R_{i3}$, $W_i$ on the recording grid.

nodes.name: Reduction to synchronous case
nodes.statement:
As 
\[{\bf W}_{i} = \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) \Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^*,
\]
and 
\[
\Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^* = \begin{pmatrix}
X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(1)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(1)}\\
 \vdots\\
  X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(p)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(p)}\\
  \end{pmatrix},
\]
it reduces to the synchronous setting.
nodes.statement_short: $W_i$ is a synchronous pre-averaged return.

nodes.name: Scale of W_i
nodes.statement:
Using a similar argument to that in \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, we have
\[ \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
nodes.statement_short: $3\sum|W_i|^2/p\to\theta$.

nodes.name: Two remaining bounds
nodes.statement_short: Need a lower bound on $|W_i|^2$ and uniform smallness of remainders.

nodes.name: Noisy and latent share LSD
nodes.statement: Hence, the PA-ATVA matrix based on noisy observations $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^*_{2i}$ and that based on latent log price $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}$ have the same LSD.
nodes.statement_short: Then noisy and latent asynchronous PA-ATVA share an LSD.

nodes.name: Apply perturbation lemma
nodes.statement:
Further, using \eqref{eq: min of Wi2}, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, and Lemma \ref{lem: appendix B lemma 1}, we obtain that
\[
3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p} \cdot \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^* (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}
~~\text{and}~~3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD, and
\[
\lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p}=  \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma D.1 transfers LSD and scale from $W_i$ to asynchronous returns.

nodes.name: Apply Xia-Zheng Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
Moreover, the LSD of  $3 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_{i}|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}$ is generated by Theorem 2.3 of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}.
Therefore, the proof of Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA asynt} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: The synchronous LSD is given by Xia-Zheng Theorem 2.3; theorem follows.

nodes.name: Remaining bounds
nodes.statement: Finally, we only need to show the proofs of \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} and \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the two remaining bounds.

nodes.name: Lower bound on W_i
nodes.statement: Notice that \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} follows naturally from the proof of \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound as in Lemma B.1.

nodes.name: Moments of remainders
nodes.statement:
To prove \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, by the normality of $R_{i1}^{(q)}$, $R_{i2}^{(q)}$, and $R_{i3}^{(q)}$, Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}, and $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n, 1\leq q\leq  p} nh(s_{T_i}^{(q)} - t_i) \to 0 $ almost surely, we have
\[
E(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),
\]
\[E(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\]
and
\[E(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Means and variances of the remainders are small.

nodes.name: High moment bound
nodes.statement:
Let $R_{i}^{(q)} = R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$; thus, by $C_p$ inequality and the normality of $R_{i}^{(q)} $, we have for any $\kappa\geq 1$, 
\[
 E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) < Cn^{-1} ~~\text{and}~~ E|R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa} \leq Cn^{-\kappa},
\]
for all $i, q$.
nodes.statement_short: $C_p$ inequality and normality give $2\kappa$-moment bounds.

nodes.name: Union bound with Markov
nodes.statement:
Hence,  it follows that for any $\varepsilon >0$ and $\kappa \geq 1$,
\[
\begin{split}
&P\left(\max\limits_{i,q} \sqrt{p}| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |\geq \varepsilon\right) \\
&\leq \sum\limits_{i,q}\frac{p^{\kappa} E| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}}\\
&\leq C\cdot \frac{Mp\cdot p^{\kappa} \cdot n^{-\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}} = O(p^{2-\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)}).
\end{split}
\]
nodes.statement_short: Union bound plus Markov gives $O(p^{2-\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)})$.

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli
nodes.statement:
We choose $\kappa$ large enough such that $\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)- 2 > 1$.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key} holds by the Borel--Cantelli lemma.
\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\kappa$ large; Borel-Cantelli concludes.

nodes.name: Estimate scale
nodes.statement: First, the estimator $\hat{\theta}_p = 3\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2/p$ can be established based on high-frequency data during time interval $[T - 1, T]$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\hat\theta_p$ from the last day.

nodes.name: Collect increments
nodes.statement: Suppose that there are in total $M_{\tau} = \tau \cdot M$ averaged noisy increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2j}, j = 1, \cdots, M_{\tau}$, over time period $[T - \tau, T]$, in which the overnight increments are excluded and there are $M$ increments each day.
nodes.statement_short: Collect $M_\tau$ pre-averaged increments, excluding overnight.

nodes.name: Permutation loop
nodes.statement:
Next, we permute the increments $B$ times.
At the $k$th permutation, we split the increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}$ into two parts, say $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)} = (\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_1, \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_2)$, for $k = 1,\cdots, B$, with $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_\ell$ having size $p\times M_{\tau_{\ell}}$ $(\ell = 1, 2)$ and $M_{\tau_1} + M_{\tau_2} = M_{\tau}$.
We define
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_{\ell}^{(k)} := \frac{p}{M_{\tau_{\ell}}}\sum_{i \in J_{\ell, k}}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2},
\]
where $J_{\ell, k} = \{i: \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} \in \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{\ell}^{(k)}\}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$ and $k = 1, \cdots, B$.
We denote the spectral decomposition of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)}$ as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_1^{(k)}(\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
for $k = 1,\cdots, B$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat $B$ random permutations.

nodes.name: Average and rescale
nodes.statement_short: Average the split estimators and multiply by $\hat\theta_p$.

nodes.name: Choose split size
nodes.statement_short: Choose $M_{\tau_1}$ from a candidate grid minimizing a Frobenius criterion.

nodes.name: Split data
nodes.statement: At the $k$th permutation, we split the increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}$ into two parts, say $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)} = (\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_1, \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_2)$, for $k = 1,\cdots, B$, with $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_\ell$ having size $p\times M_{\tau_{\ell}}$ $(\ell = 1, 2)$ and $M_{\tau_1} + M_{\tau_2} = M_{\tau}$.
nodes.statement_short: Split permuted increments into two parts.

nodes.name: Split matrices
nodes.statement:
We define
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_{\ell}^{(k)} := \frac{p}{M_{\tau_{\ell}}}\sum_{i \in J_{\ell, k}}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2},
\]
where $J_{\ell, k} = \{i: \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} \in \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{\ell}^{(k)}\}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$ and $k = 1, \cdots, B$.
nodes.statement_short: Form self-normalized matrices on each part.

nodes.name: Eigendecompose first part
nodes.statement:
We denote the spectral decomposition of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)}$ as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_1^{(k)}(\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
for $k = 1,\cdots, B$.
nodes.statement_short: Eigendecompose the first split's matrix.

nodes.name: Eigenvectors from past days
nodes.statement:
First, the matrix $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T-1}$ in \eqref{eq: definition of hbSigma} is constructed based on high-frequency data during time period $[T - \tau, T - 1]$, and its spectral decomposition is denoted as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T-\tau, T - 1}(\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where
\[
\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[1], \cdots, \widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[p]).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Eigendecompose $\widetilde\Xi$ built on $[T-\tau,T-1]$.

nodes.name: Project last day's data
nodes.statement:
Second, we set the eigenvectors $\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[k]$, $k = 1,\cdots, p$, to be given beforehand, and transform the averaged high-frequency data $\{\overline{{\bf Y}}_i\}$ during time period $[T - 1, T]$.
That is, consider $\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[k])^{{\mathrm{T}}}\overline{{\bf Y}}_i$ as the transformed averaged observations at recording time $t_i \in [T - 1,T]$, for $k = 1,\cdots, p, i = 0,\cdots, n$.
nodes.statement_short: Project last day's averaged prices onto the eigenvectors.

nodes.name: Averaging-pre-averaging volatility
nodes.statement:
Third, for each $k = 1,\cdots, p$, compute the averaging-pre-averaging estimator 
\[
\widehat{d_i^{\textrm{APA}}} = \frac{12}{k_n }\sum_{i = 0}^{n - k_n + 1}(\Delta_{i,k_n}^k\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} )^2 - \frac{6}{\vartheta^2 n} \sum_{i = 0}^{n-1} (\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + 1}^{**} - \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**})^2,
\]
where $k_n = \lfloor \vartheta n^{1/2}\rfloor,  \vartheta>0$ and $\Delta_{i,k_n}^k\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**} = \sum_{j = 1}^{k_n -1} g(j/k_n)( \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + j + 1}^{**} - \overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i + j}^{**})$ with $g(x) = x\wedge (1-x)$, which is a consistent estimator of the integrated volatility of $(\overline{{\bf Y}}_{k, i}^{**})$ over $[T - 1, T]$ by given ${\bf U}_{T - \tau, T - 1}$, see \cite{Jacodetal2009} and \cite{Liuetal2018}.
nodes.statement_short: Estimate each projected integrated volatility by the APA estimator.

nodes.name: Assemble MNS
nodes.statement:
Finally, our mixed nonlinear shrinkage (MNS) estimator of ICV is defined as
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\textrm{MNS}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1} \textrm{diag} (\widehat{d_1^{\textrm{APA}}}, \cdots, \widehat{d_p^{\textrm{APA}}})\widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1}^{{\mathrm{T}}}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine eigenvectors with estimated eigenvalues.
